source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #261 (#195, pack compiled functions into dual-view code slabs). The PR rewrites CodeArena in crates/telomere-jit-codegen/src/code_memory.rs: compiled functions are bump-allocated at 16-byte alignment into 256 KiB dual-view slabs (one shared backing mapped RW and RX; the RW view is permanently unmapped when a slab fills or seals, keeping the W^X contract one-way; oversized functions get a dedicated slab; environments without a shared backing fall back to the previous per-function mapping), adds a cfg(unix) libc dependency to telomere-jit-codegen, switches the JIT cache accounting in crates/telomere/src/runtime/jit/cache.rs from page-rounded sizes to accounted_len (aligned code bytes), and adds aarch64 instruction-cache flushes (__clear_cache on Linux, sys_icache_invalidate on macOS). A follow-up commit casts the shm_open mode through c_uint so the macOS build compiles (mode_t is u16 there and cannot be passed to the variadic shm_open; E0617). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (133bf4b) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45091421967, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 28 gated series, so every delta is this PR’s own. Only the core-jit configuration links telomere-jit-codegen into the minimal embedder, so the delta is confined to its 4 gated series: release stripped file +3,072 B / stripped .text +2,320 B; release-size stripped file +1,872 B / stripped .text +1,248 B. The other 24 gated series are byte-identical. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
